test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A gut feeling
solution:
The correct answer is "**An instinct or intuition**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given options, **"An instinct or intuition"** is the appropriate meaning of the idiom.
 
• We use the idiom - A gut feeling to mean **'an instinctive feeling**'.
 
 
• **Example: ** I have** a gut feeling** that something bad is going to happen.
 
 
 
• Thus, ***option 2) ***is the correct alternative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let us see few more idioms and their meaning.

 
• When pigs fly – something that will never happen.

 
 
• **Example:** When pigs fly she’ll clean up her room.
 
 
 
• **Break a leg **– means ‘good luck’ (often said to actors before they go on stage).
 
 
• **Example:** Break a leg Sam, I’m sure your performance will be great. 
 
 
 
• ​Stealing someone's thunder– Taking credit for someone else achievements.
 
• To hit the nail on the head – to describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.
 
 
• **Example: **“He hit the nail on the head when he said this company needs more HR support.”
